title: EJBCA Certificate Enrollment Error (Not Allow Signature Algorithm Different from CA)
body_text:
I have a question about when I use different Signature Algorithm Certificate profile against form CA_x000D_
Such like CA is using SHA512ECDSA and Certificate profile is setting up to SHA256RSA_x000D_
will get the enrollment error below_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
EJBCA Certificate Enrollment Error_x000D_
Username: _x000D_
Request failed. org.bouncycastle.operator.OperatorCreationException: cannot create signer: Supplied key_x000D_
(org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.asymmetric.ec.BCECPrivateKey) is not a RSAPrivateKey instance_x000D_
```
top_3_comments_text: primetomas: Hi, This is as it should be. If the CA has an EC key, it can not sign with an RSA signature algorithm. A CA that has an EC key, i.e. Root CA that has signed itself with ECDSA, can only issue certificates signed using an ECDSA signature algorithm. This is the nature of the cryptography. Set the Certificate Profile setting to SHA256WithECDSA (or SHA384WithECDSA or SHA512WithECDSA)... Cheers, Tomas

title: WARNING: An illegal reflective access operation has occurred
body_text:
Greetings colleagues._x000D_
It turns out that I am implementing the primekey/ejbca-ce image in a virtualized environment. I cloned the virtual server where I have it running and when I lift the container on the new server I get this error in the logs: _x000D_
WARNING: An illegal reflective access operation has occurred..._x000D_
I can access the public web via http but I cannot access the interface via https. _x000D_
I will appreciate any suggestions _x000D_
Thanks_x000D_
![error an illegal reflective access](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49497727/144940470-b7d03132-3d7c-4c3b-9598-59f0d79d9bd4.png)
top_3_comments_text: primetomas: That is a warning from WildFly, not EJBCA. It's nothing to care about. You are using WildFly 22, so my guess is that the https/tls settings are not right. WildFly 22: https://doc.primekey.com/ejbca/ejbca-installation/application-servers/wildfly-22-jboss-eap-7-4 | blancoreyes: > That is a warning from WildFly, not EJBCA. It's nothing to care about. > > You are using WildFly 22, so my guess is that the https/tls settings are not right. WildFly 22: https://doc.primekey.com/ejbca/ejbca-installation/application-servers/wildfly-22-jboss-eap-7-4 Aren't those parameters supposed to be set automatic when the bin is first lifted? | primetomas: I'm not sure what parameters you are referring to? The bin (ejbca.ear) file can not configure TLS in WildFly, you can automate it in your container for sure. The message: WARNING: An illegal reflective access operation has occurred has nothing todo with this, this is completely harmless. You need to look elsewhere in the log for the description about TLS. That is not it.
